chapter: Henry Horton and the Rhythm Club
title: Refusing a dollar-a-night drum job; Black Gold; Rhythm Club
summary: He refused drum work at a dollar a night, played the Black Gold briefly, then joined Henry Horton at the Rhythm Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I think I paid a couple of nights, at the Black Gold. And I had to leave, I had to leave the job, on account of, cursed, you know? You know? What kind of what? The only kind of what? The only kind of cursed, you know?
Oh, yeah. I thought you said spirits.
I mean, spirits, I mean, yeah.

No, no. Mm-mm. You didn't believe it. Well, I didn't, they ran out for job. I mean, I didn't want to see, I didn't want to get away, you know? I didn't want to get away, you know, And I leave there, I go to the, Jackman and Bird and the Witch, I played there, a long time, you could call it, you could call it up there, Jackman and Bird and up there, until he, built the place up, and he named it the Rhythm Club.

Henry Horton. I was playing up there with Henry Horton, myself, Doug McCullum, Andrew Horton. Who was fantastic at the home? I'd get those hands, who was fancy, you know, and John that's saying. We had a 17th band, but we could use two trumpets. He's telling the same. Can't think about who was playing piano with us up there. We had quite a few piano players, can't buy it. Well, we played upstairs, and saw Jackman doing this, and caught it, Jackman did, or when they, when they made the Rhythm Club. Well, we'd throw it up upstairs, become Melonstadt. Well, Henry Horton, Thornton, Lord, and his band, started putting on one saxophone, and, and there was a trumpet. Now, they got his band up to 12 men, that's what the average band was carrying at that time. I don't think we had no trumpet, no chime on the play after, I can't remember, I don't believe. Well, I played at the Rhythm Club, we played there, and Henry Horton used to broadcast every night, and WJSU, at 10 o'clock. I stayed there, I think I stayed there about a year and a half, two years. I was now, I'm about 37. 37 or 38, I think at 37.
